analysis.title: Investors' Outlook: Over the peak (November 2026)
key_insights: Vontobel expects economic growth, inflation and 10-year US Treasury yields to have peaked, and sees 2027 as flatter terrain with slower growth and possibly lower inflation. Fading fiscal support, especially in the US, is expected to sap demand.

October saw a government bond sell-off that pushed yields higher and spilled into equities. A tech-driven correction later in the month prompted a flight to safety that lifted bond prices. Bonds outperformed equities for the first time in a while.

The Multi Asset Investment Committee tilted slightly more defensive. It moved high yield bonds from overweight to neutral and upgraded government bonds from underweight to neutral. Overweights in equities, emerging-market stocks and gold are unchanged, and the overall bond stance stays underweight.

The AI-driven tech sell-off had four causes: hotter US inflation pushing yields to two-decade highs, worries about debt-funded AI financing, CXMT memory-chip progress raising pricing-power concerns (hit South Korea and Taiwan hardest), and crowded positioning in a few AI winners. Chipmakers logged their longest losing streak since 2008.

Vontobel says the AI cycle has not peaked. Demand is strong, results confirm computing power is scarce, and investors now favor companies that fund spending from their own profits. The S&P 500 forward P/E fell from about 25x to below 20x, and Vontobel sees limited room for further compression, so earnings must drive returns.
Defensive sectors (staples, energy, health care) and quality and low-volatility styles outperformed during the tech sell-off, and the average stock held up better than the major indices.

Central banks have tightened. The ECB raised rates by a cumulative 50 bps to a 2.50% deposit rate. The Fed hiked 25 bps in September to 3.75-4.00%. The BoJ policy rate is at a 31-year high of 1.25%. The 10-year US Treasury yield is up over 100 bps in 2026 and has breached 5%.

The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% on October 28 with two members favoring a 25 bp hike. The Fed's median projection shows rates flat in 2027, while markets price close to two more hikes. Vontobel thinks the market is more likely to move toward the Fed.

Almost all of this year's rise in 10-year yields is higher real yields rather than higher inflation compensation or term premium. Vontobel calls it an oil shock filtered through the expected Fed response, which can reverse. The main risk is doubt about the Fed's resolve, which would hit longer maturities most.

At around 5%, 10-year Treasuries offer attractive asymmetry in Vontobel's view. Over 12 months a yield rise of about 75 bps could be absorbed before a USD investor loses money, while a 100 bp fall implies a return above 12%. These are illustrations, not forecasts.

High yield spreads have widened, with stress spreading from CCC to BB and B. Yields are around 8%, and Vontobel moved to neutral while favoring BB. Investment-grade spreads are thin, AI-related issuance is set to resume (Microsoft bond sale planned), and returns should come from carry and rates rather than tighter spreads.

Housing is an early sign of strain. The 30-year US mortgage rate passed 7.6% in late October and mortgage applications fell. Vontobel's base case is slower growth, not recession, because households have lower leverage, real oil prices are below past crisis levels, and the AI capex cycle, defense spending and supply-chain reshoring support activity.

Inflation drivers in 2026 were tariffs, the Middle East energy shock and AI investment. Vontobel expects energy and tariff effects to fade in 2027. San Francisco Fed cyclical core PCE has not reaccelerated and 5y5y inflation swaps are well anchored, so it expects the tightening cycle to have limited longevity. The next meaningful labor-market deterioration could be the catalyst to end it.

Oil: Vontobel's base case for 2027 is gradual normalization, with firmer prices in H1 and softer in H2. The IEA estimates 2026 global oil demand fell about 2.5-2.6 mb/d. Consensus expects a swing from deficit to surplus in 2027, but restocking (the US SPR is near its lowest since 1982) should keep prices supported in H1.

EUR/USD fell from just above 1.20 in January to about 1.12. The France-Germany 10-year spread is near euro-crisis highs, and Vontobel attributes most of the widening to French budget politics. It sees a French problem, not a euro crisis, and expects EUR/USD at 1.10-1.15 until a budget passes.

The dollar's rebound is seen as a rates-driven bounce, not a new uptrend. Markets expect the dollar's rate advantage to peak in H1 2027 and then narrow. The SNB policy rate is at zero, and the yield gap likely caps further Swiss franc gains.

Gold traded around USD 4,100-4,200 per ounce in October, pressured by higher yields and real rates. Vontobel keeps its overweight, viewing the pressure as temporary, with official-sector purchases as structural support.

sector_views.rationale: Labor markets resilient, earnings holding up, AI investment strong, yields stabilizing, positioning less stretched.
Overweight unchanged. AI and tech cycle supports Asian exporters, and earnings forecasts are rising.
Upgraded from underweight. Attractive yields, duration added ahead of softer 2027 growth and inflation, and a hedge against recession.
Cut from overweight. Growth expected to slow and spreads look tight relative to volatility. BB favored.
Pressure from yields seen as temporary. Official purchases and geopolitical uncertainty support it.
Moderating growth into 2027 justifies neutral, though they act as an inflation hedge during supply shocks.
Gained during the October tech sell-off. Vontobel notes concentration risk in portfolios heavy in a few large caps.

earnings_insights: Global earnings growth forecasts for 2027 EPS have continued to rise across the US, Eurozone, Japan and emerging markets, per Vontobel's Chart 2 (LSEG data as of October 22, 2026).
Vontobel says the latest company results confirm computing power is in short supply. The gap between companies with strong profits and cash and those reliant on outside financing is widening.

trade_ideas.description: Add duration through 10-year US Treasuries at around 5% yield
trade_ideas.rationale: Potential gains from a fall in yields appear larger than potential losses, and government bonds hedge recession risk.
trade_ideas.risk: Doubt about the Fed's resolve could weigh most on longer maturities.

trade_ideas.description: Move high yield bonds from overweight to neutral and favor BB-rated credit
trade_ideas.rationale: Growth is poised to slow, and spreads look tight relative to volatility.
Yield pressure is temporary, and official-sector purchases and geopolitical uncertainty support it.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher bond yields and real rates raise the opportunity cost of holding gold.

risk_factors: Geopolitics is the main upside risk to inflation and downside risk to growth, including a Middle East escalation or other supply shock.
Fiscal sustainability in the US, France or the UK could trigger higher bond yields and tighter financial conditions.
Central banks may be overestimating how much restrictive policy the economy can bear, and rate-sensitive sectors like housing could spill over into consumption, investment and employment.
An AI-related downturn from slower spending, weaker commercial adoption or a competing region's breakthrough.
Doubt about the Fed's resolve could hit longer maturities most.
OPEC+ cohesion could be tested, which could push oil lower than expected.
A French downgrade or failed budget vote could push EUR/USD toward the low end of 1.10-1.15.
charts_described: Chart 5 plots the San Francisco Fed 1-month and 12-month cyclical core PCE inflation. The text says the measure has kept inching lower and has not reaccelerated.
Chart 4 shows real Brent prices in constant 2026 dollars. The text says they sit well below levels seen in past energy crises.
Chart 2 (US Treasuries) shows approximate 1-year total return against the 10-year yield move in bps. The text says a rise of about 75 bps could be absorbed before a loss.
Chart 1 (bonds) shows the market-implied Fed path against the Fed dots. The text says the gap is in 2027, where the Fed projects flat rates and markets price close to two further hikes.
vol_and_positioning: Vontobel expects volatility to stay elevated.
Crowded positioning in a small group of AI winners amplified the October decline. Sentiment and positioning have since become less stretched.
Credit spreads look tight relative to volatility, which is why Vontobel moved high yield to neutral.
geopolitical: Iran-aligned Houthi forces claimed attacks on Saudi Arabian energy and civilian infrastructure, which sent Brent well above USD 100 per barrel.
Trump threatened to curb diesel exports and secured Europe's agreement to coordinate the release of part of its diesel reserves.
Trump suspended parts of a Russia sanctions package days before it was due to take effect.

Vontobel expects Democrats to take control of Congress in the November 3 US midterms. It warns that Trump may turn attention abroad afterward, raising the risk of tariff threats or Middle East escalation.
The Strait of Hormuz was temporarily closed in 2026.
French government bond spreads over Bunds are near euro-crisis highs on budget deficit and political pressure ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

tension_points.bull_case: Fed's median projection shows rates flat in 2027, and Vontobel expects the market to move toward the Fed as energy-driven inflation fades. Government bonds then gain from lower yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets price close to two further hikes in 2027, and sticky core services inflation or doubt about the Fed's resolve could keep yields higher, hitting longer maturities most.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If sticky core services inflation does not ease, the extra 2027 hikes stay priced in. Doubt about the Fed's resolve would also undermine the view.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand is strong, computing power is short, earnings forecasts keep rising and yields are stabilizing, so the October sell-off is a healthy adjustment.
tension_points.bear_case: AI financing is debt-heavy, CXMT progress threatens memory pricing power, positioning is crowded and inflation could stay sticky, which could drive a deeper correction.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A slowdown in AI spending, weaker commercial adoption, or a breakthrough by competing regions.

tension_points.bull_case: The strain is confined to French bonds, ECB stress measures are near historic lows, and a credible budget could quickly remove part of the risk premium.
tension_points.bear_case: The deficit is around 5% of GDP, parliament is fragmented, and the spread is near euro-crisis highs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A downgrade of France's credit rating or a failed budget vote would push the euro toward the low end of the 1.10-1.15 range.
